title: Malthusian Cat
text: We had a cat in our house, which ought to have belonged to Mr Malthus. Her first litter of kittens was drowned, excepting one, which she brought up. Of the next litter, one was also preserved: but the cat had no further desire to experience the transports of maternal love; for, the first time she saw the servant standing by a pail of water, she brought the kitten in her mouth, and laid it beside it, looking up, as much as to say, "put it in:" and from that time never would nurse it. -Literary Gazette. [We doubt this story].
